answer: The quill multiplier is published, charged in thread, and whisper lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 5 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1212 identities would post 2206 proofs and burn roughly 24 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
